_comment: Per-skill content guards — load-bearing markers that must survive customization. Each guard passes if ANY of its regexes matches the installed skill (Python re.search over the whole file, no flags — so `.` does not cross newlines and ^/$ are string anchors). Ported from sync.sh so the check outlives it; build-index.sh folds these into registry.json, and /skill uses them in `add` self-validation and `outdated`. WRITING A GUARD: bind the sentence that states the rule, not a word that happens to appear near it. Every alternate in an `anyOf` must be a rewording of the SAME sentence — never a neighbouring heading, table row, or output template, because those are exactly what survives when a customizing agent rewrites the rule. The code that ENACTS a rule is not an alternate either — a `gh issue create` invocation, a jq filter, a `git pull` — because an `anyOf` is an OR, so one surviving code alternate reinstates the vacuity the prose alternates were added to fix; bind the sentence and drop the command. Validate by deleting ONLY the rule line and leaving the decoration intact: if the guard still matches, it is vacuous. Note that `guard-audit.py` cannot see the case where a skill DOCUMENTS its own rule in prose elsewhere (a "Why This Works" bullet restating a rule that lives in a snippet) — that one only shows up under the deletion test. An optional `note` field records why a non-obvious pattern is shaped the way it is; skill-lint and /skill read only `label` and `anyOf`. An optional `gate` field on a guard object is that guard's entry in the gate ledger (docs/gate-ledger-shape.md) — the failure mode it targets and the evidence chain that justified it — and is likewise ignored by skill-lint and /skill.

Now binds the sentence that states the rule — a valid-but-out-of-scope finding becomes a tracked GitHub issue, never just a review comment. The command is the ENACTMENT, not the rule: a copy that keeps a `gh issue create` snippet after deleting the instruction has lost the rule, so it is deliberately not an alternate. Distinct from `mandatory-issues`, which binds that the rule is mandatory rather than what it requires. The first cut of this bind was too NARROW: it turned two installed copies red that state the rule perfectly well (exodus-loop "MUST get a tracked GitHub issue" under a "NOTHING IS LOST." lead; repo-relay "Create GitHub issue for everything else (MANDATORY - nothing gets lost)"). A bare `nothing gets lost` slogan was tried first and REJECTED: it matched "Nothing gets lost when the build cache is warm", so it could have held the guard green off prose that says nothing about deferred findings — the same vacuity this guard was rebound to fix. Every alternate is a clause about what happens to a deferred finding.

Now binds the RULE SENTENCE — "The reviewer's final report MUST end with a fenced ```json review-result``` block" — via a pattern tolerant of the 4-backtick escaping the sentence itself needs to display 3 backticks inline. Verified both ways: deleting only that sentence (leaving the fence, the JSON example, the field docs, and the record-command prose intact, and `review-result` still appearing 6 of its original 8 times) turns the guard red; restoring it turns the guard green.

EVERY alternate binds the SCOPE CLAUSE — that the ceiling includes the refute/verify agents — not merely the number 20 near the word 'ceiling'. That is deliberate and is the whole point: the historical breach was not someone deleting the cap, it was someone reading it as panel-only, and an alternate like `20 is a hard ceiling` stays GREEN on '20 is a hard ceiling on the workhorse panel; refute/verify agents are counted separately'. Requiring an INCLUSION word (includes/counting/stays within) adjacent to the refuter noun is what separates the rule from that mutant, which also mentions refuters — in order to exclude them. Kept SEPARATE from refuters-per-finding-cap so stripping either half fails. Single-line by necessity: guards are re.search with no flags, and full-review.md wraps this sentence across a newline, so alternate 2 binds its second line. Verified: all six templates match, six rule-gutting mutants (panel-only x2, inversion, scope-dropped, soft-target, 20->40) all go red, no line outside the six templates matches, and deleting only the rule line fails every alternate.

visual-brief.label: dark-by-default-no-light-flip
visual-brief.note:
Replaces #135's respects-reader-colour-scheme, which REQUIRED a prefers-color-scheme light flip. The owner asked for dark reports on 2026-09-24 ('so it wasn't so bright and hard on the eyes'): the Claude app's browser pane renders local HTML in LIGHT mode whatever the OS setting, so following prefers-color-scheme gave a glaring white brief. The invariant is now two-sided and one regex carries both halves, because anyOf is an OR and two alternates could each pass alone: (1) a dark-only declaration ':root{color-scheme:dark;' is present — ':root{' with the brace, so the inert ':root[data-theme="light"]' block cannot satisfy it, and 'dark;' with the semicolon, so #135's 'dark light;' cannot; (2) the leading lookahead rejects any @media rule that keys prefers-color-scheme:light and opens a brace, spanning newlines but only over media-query characters ([\s\w(),:.-]). A backtick, quote, em dash, semicolon or '<' ends the span, and that is what lets prose QUOTE the old query without tripping the guard. The first version of this guard confined the span to one line instead, and so passed a flip written across lines (found by Copilot on PR #306). Proven red on: the origin/main #135 skeleton verbatim; 'dark' widened to 'dark light'; the light block re-keyed to @media (prefers-color-scheme:light) with the dark declaration kept; the dark declaration deleted; a light default with a prefers dark flip; the '@media screen and (...: light) {' spelling; and that flip split across lines three ways ('@media
(...)
{', 'only screen and
(...) {', '(...) and (min-width: 37.5em)
{'). Green on the ported skeleton and on prose naming the old query, backtick-quoted or not, placed BEFORE the skeleton so that a later brace exists. Like #135's guard it binds the CODE, because the skeleton is the artifact every brief is generated from: deleting only the 'Dark, always, by default' prose bullet leaves it green, and that is correct rather than vacuous — the output is still dark.

anyOf: Hotspots are files touched by at least max\(4, 5% of the run's PRs\) merged PRs, and top-level packages by PR count, printed with the threshold\.

anyOf: Leave out lockfiles, generated files \(including those marked in `\.gitattributes`\), and version and changelog files\.

run-report.label: unreached-channel-undelivered

run-report.label: deploy-needs-readback

run-report.label: no-skip-on-judgement

run-report.label: run-record-at-start

run-report.label: records-stay-private
anyOf: They stay in their private directories and never go into a repository, issue or PR\.

run-report.label: no-authority
anyOf: It adds no gate and no authority, and it never changes a review or a merge posture\.

run-report.label: mid-run-brief-not-stop

run-report.label: recording-never-blocks

run-report.label: backfill-reconstructed

run-report.label: done-or-stop-at-merge
